blocks.text: Autonomous Application Shield uses AI to identify risks in private applications in the Zscaler Admin Console. Private applications are scanned based on a specific scanning intensity and time, and these scan reports are forwarded to the Zscaler cloud AI system. Zscaler uses this information to learn new attack techniques, which helps to evolve private application protection. Existing AppProtection controls are then assigned to application segments to monitor or block vulnerabilities.

Before using Autonomous Application Shield, make sure that you have designated App Connectors as App Scanners, created a scan profile, and created a scan. After these prerequisites are complete and scans begin for applications, you can review the data from the scans on the Autonomous Application Shield page.
Autonomous Application Shield provides the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Scan, detect, and respond to private application risks in minutes via an autonomous setup, resulting in efficient, streamlined responses to threats.
Reduce the exposure time of risk and keep up with application changes.
Determine which AppProtection control is needed for each application based on the detected threats and vulnerabilities.

blocks.heading: About the Autonomous Application Shield Protection Page

blocks.text: On the Autonomous Application Shield page (Private Access > Autonomous App Shield > Shield), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Click Protection to view the threat severities for applications in an application segment. This option is selected by default.
Click Scan Status to see the statuses and details for existing scans.
Refresh the Autonomous Application Shield Protection page to reflect the most current information.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Click the Filters icon to show or hide filters.
Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. To learn more, see Using Tables.
View a list of application segments. For each application segment, you can view:
Application Segment: The application segment that was scanned for threats using Autonomous Application Shield.
Click an application segment to view its AppProtection controls.
Control Name: The name of the AppProtection control. Click the AppProtection control name to open the Assessment Findings drawer. This drawer includes the following information:
CVE ID: The identification number for the CVE.
Vulnerability: The name of the vulnerability detected.
Description: The description of the detected vulnerability.
Detected Date: The date that the vulnerability was detected.
Severity: The level of the threat identified.
CVSS: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) score.
See image.
Control Type: The type of AppProtection control (Predefined or ThreatLabZ).
Severity: The level of the threat identified.
Status: The status of the AppProtection control (e.g., Deployed).
Applications Count: The number of applications using the AppProtection control.
CVEs Count: The number of common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVE) that have been detected.
See image.
Applications: The applications associated with the scan.
Severity: The threat severity levels that were found while scanning the applications.
Recommended Controls Count: The number of recommended AppProtection controls.
Deployed Controls Count: The number of AppProtection controls deployed for the scan.
Click the Shield Profile icon to review the details of the AppProtection controls that are addressing the threats.
Click to view details on the Configure Protection page
Application Segment Name: The name of the application segment.
Auto Application Shield: This option is enabled by default. Click Disabled to disable the Auto Application Shield feature from the application segment.
Control Name: The name of the AppProtection control. Click the application segment name to open the Assessment Findings drawer. This drawer includes the following information:
CVE ID: The identification number for the CVE.
Vulnerability: The name of the vulnerability detected.
Description: The description of the vulnerability that was detected.
Detected Date: The date that the vulnerability was detected.
Severity: The level of the threat identified.
CVSS: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) score.
See image.
Control Type: The type of AppProtection control (Predefined or ThreatLabZ).
Severity: The level of the threat identified.
Status: The status of the AppProtection Control (e.g., Deployed).
Action: The action assigned to the AppProtection control in response to the threat.
Monitor: The AppProtection control monitors the applications associated with that threat.
Block: The AppProtection control blocks the applications associated with that threat.
Applications Count: The number of applications using the AppProtection control.
CVEs Count: The number of common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVE) that have been detected.
See image.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.

blocks.heading: About the Autonomous Application Shield Scan Status Page

blocks.text: On the Autonomous Application Shield page (Private Access > Autonomous App Shield > Shield), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Click Download Report to download the scan report in either a CSV or PDF format.
Click Protection to view the threat severities for applications in an application segment. This option is selected by default.
Click Scan Status to see the statuses and details for existing scans.
Refresh the Autonomous Application Shield Scan Status page to reflect the most current information.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Click the Filters icon again to show or hide filters.
Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. To learn more, see Using Tables.
View a list of application segments. For each application segment, you can view:
Application Segment: The application segment that was scanned for threats using Autonomous Application Shield.
Click an application segment to view its App Scanners.

Application: The application that was scanned for threats using Autonomous Application Shield. Click the application to open the Assessment Findings drawer. This drawer includes the following information:
CVE ID: The identification number for the CVE.
Vulnerability: The name of the vulnerability detected.
Description: The description of the detected vulnerability.
Detected Date: The date that the vulnerability was detected.
Severity: The level of the threat identified.
CVSS: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) score.
See image.
Status: The status of the scan.
App Scanner: The associated App Scanner for the scan.
Scan Interval: When the scan began and ended.
CVEs Count: The number of CVEs that have been detected.
See image.
Scan ID: The identification number for the scan.
Status: The status of the scan.
Start Time: The time the scan began.
End Time: The time the scan ended.
Applications: The applications associated with the scan.
CVEs Count: The number of CVEs that have been detected.
Click the Download icon to download the scan information details into a JSON file.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
